messages:
maria: quick heads-up — ran FlashAttention v3 canary against our perf harness this morning. mixed results depending on seq distribution.

sam: details? numbers?

maria: pasted rough snapshot below (all on p4d-ish infra, bf16):
```
model: llama-13b
batch sizes: 4,8,16
seqs tested: 8,64,512,2048
v2 median token/s: 1200 / 3800 / 7200 / 5200
v3 median token/s: 1100 / 4100 / 9200 / 6400
p99 latency (ms) @ seq=8: v2=18.3 v3=22.1
p99 latency @ seq=2048: v2=410 v3=320
```

anya: interesting — v3 wins at long seqs and throughput, but tail at short seqs got worse. did you sample mixed-length batches?

maria: yes. the worst p99s were when we had mixed short+long in same batch (e.g., one seq=2048, others=8). v3 appears to allocate larger workspaces that thrash for small tokens.

lee: that sounds like workspace reuse issue. v3 preallocates a single big buffer keyed by max_seq in batch. with heterogeneous batches we pay for the big buffer + kernel warmup. v2 had smaller per-item allocations and could inplace fallback.

sam: do we see any correctness/overflow errors?

maria: one run hit a workspace-exhausted warning and triggered our fallback to aten for that request. logs:
```
[2026-03-18T09:12:22Z] WARN flashattn_v3: workspace_required=1.2GB available=1.0GB -> fallback to cpu-fallback/aten
[2026-03-18T09:12:22Z] INFO request 0x7fae3: routed to aten fallback
```

tim: deploy-bot, did the canary rollout record any impact to SLOs?

deploy-bot: Canary rollout started 2026-03-18T08:00:00Z. 2% traffic. No SLO breaches on error rate. Latency trend: p50 unchanged, p95 +3%, p99 +8% in canary cohort.

anya: +8% p99 aligns with maria's short-seq observations. We need heuristic selection in the kernel selector rather than pure prefer-v3.

sam: propose selector rules like:
```
# pseudo-config for kernel selection
kernel_selector:
  prefer: flashattn_v3
  fallbacks: [flashattn_v2, aten]
  heuristics:
    - condition: max_seq <= 32
      prefer: flashattn_v2
    - condition: batch_homogeneous and max_seq >= 256
      prefer: flashattn_v3
    - condition: mixed_short_and_long
      prefer: flashattn_v2
    - condition: workspace_allocation_failure
      action: fallback
```

lee: can we implement a cheap runtime check: compute batch_seq_stddev and if > threshold mark mixed? that avoids parsing all lengths.

maria: yes, seq_stddev > 150 was a good proxy in my runs. but need to tune per-model.

anya: also watch quantized models: v3 shows a small correctness delta with int8 kernels when combined with rotary slicing — not huge but present. we should disable v3 for quantized until we validate.

sam: good call. add a flag in model profile: supported_kernels: [flashattn_v2, aten] for quantized=true.

maria: test/CI notes: ran 1k synthetic samples with mixed distribution, v3 caused 12% more fallback events. when we force homogeneous batches, v3 improved throughput by 1.3x median at seq 512+.

anya: action items:
- sam: land kernel-selector config + cheap seq_stddev heuristic (PR)
- maria: run expanded perf harness for 10 models (1k runs each) and upload artifact
- lee: monitor memory fragmentation counters during canary (add metric)
- tim: coordinate canary increase only after perf CI green and memory metrics stable

sam: ok i'll start a small PR that wires selectors into request router. will default to v2 for safety behind a feature flag.

maria: one more wrinkle — v3's kernel choices change based on workspace alignment; small changes in batch ordering changed perf 6-10%. worth adding microbench reproducibility notes in the RFC.

lee: we should add a scheduled job to run stable harness nightly for the kernel matrix (v2, v3, aten) per model. that'll give us regression alerts.

anya: +1. also add e2e prompt quality checks because quant + kernel changes can produce subtle tokenization/regression differences.

tim: I'll hold the canary scale-up. ping me when PRs and perf artifacts are linked.

maria: linking artifacts in thread once finished. thanks all. :thumbsup:

sam: cool. tagging @eng-sre and @eng-runtime for visibility.

deploy-bot: Canary rollout note: increment paused pending manual approval at 2026-03-18T12:00:00Z.
